challenge.exploration_summary: Explored the chi router project structure. The middleware package contains many HTTP middleware utilities including content type validation (AllowContentType), content encoding, compression, authentication, logging, etc. The content_type.go file has AllowContentType which validates content types against a whitelist but doesn't enforce that a Content-Type header must be present. This is a gap that the new feature fills.
challenge.feature_spec: Added two new middleware functions to middleware/content_type.go: (1) RequireContentType - enforces that a Content-Type header is present on requests with a body, returning 415 Unsupported Media Type if missing. (2) RequireContentTypeWithAllowed - combines RequireContentType and AllowContentType functionality, requiring both that a Content-Type header is present AND that it matches one of the allowed content types. Both middlewares skip the check for requests without a body (ContentLength == 0).
challenge.feature_rationale: The existing AllowContentType middleware silently passes requests with no Content-Type header when the body is empty, but for requests with a body, it rejects empty content types because the empty string won't match any allowed type. However, there was no standalone middleware to simply require that a Content-Type header is present without restricting to specific types. This is useful for APIs that want to enforce good client behavior (always specify content type) without being prescriptive about which types are allowed. The RequireContentTypeWithAllowed variant provides a convenient single-middleware solution for the common case of requiring both presence and validation.
challenge.bug_description: Changed the body-presence check from 'r.ContentLength == 0' to 'r.ContentLength <= 0' in both RequireContentType and RequireContentTypeWithAllowed. When ContentLength is -1 (unknown length, as with chunked transfer encoding), the middleware incorrectly skips the Content-Type validation entirely. An attacker can bypass content-type enforcement by sending requests with Transfer-Encoding: chunked, allowing arbitrary body content without a Content-Type header to reach downstream handlers.

findings.description: The PR was applied incorrectly: the new RequireContentType and RequireContentTypeWithAllowed functions were inserted inside the body of the existing AllowContentType function (after the w.WriteHeader call on line 42 but before its closing braces). This broke the AllowContentType function and caused the entire file to fail compilation with syntax errors. The file could not be built or used at all.

Security bypass in RequireContentType: the original PR used 'r.ContentLength <= 0' to skip the content-type check. In Go, r.ContentLength is -1 when the length is unknown (e.g., chunked transfer encoding), meaning the request DOES have a body but its size is unknown. Using '<= 0' would skip the content-type enforcement for chunked requests, allowing an attacker to bypass the middleware entirely by sending a chunked-encoded POST without a Content-Type header. Fixed to 'r.ContentLength == 0' to match the existing AllowContentType pattern, which only skips when there is explicitly no body.

Same security bypass in RequireContentTypeWithAllowed: the original PR used 'r.ContentLength <= 0' to skip the content-type check. Chunked transfer encoding sets ContentLength to -1, so a request with a body sent via chunked encoding would bypass both the content-type presence check and the allowed-list check. Fixed to 'r.ContentLength == 0'.

self_review.fix_explanation: 1. Restored the AllowContentType function to its original correct form (the PR insertion had broken it by placing new function definitions inside its body). 2. Placed the two new functions (RequireContentType and RequireContentTypeWithAllowed) after AllowContentType as proper top-level functions. 3. Changed 'r.ContentLength <= 0' to 'r.ContentLength == 0' in both new functions to prevent security bypass via chunked transfer encoding (where ContentLength is -1 but a body exists). All existing tests and feature tests pass with these fixes.
